Reviews Revamp

Cross-app review management system designed to give developers with many apps unified control over their feedback

I initiated and led the UX redesign of the reviews management experience for developers.

Starting with research to identify pain points, I designed a unified dashboard that aggregates feedback across all of a developer's apps, with filtering, sorting, response management, and an AI-assisted flow for reporting inappropriate reviews. Though not shipped, the work established a clear strategic direction for scalable cross-app review management.

Research and direction

  • I initiated this project based on research and conversations with account managers, mapping developer pain points around cross-app review management

Designing the system

  • Designed a unified dashboard aggregating reviews across all apps, with filtering, sorting, and response management
  • Moved the review-reading experience from an inline accordion to a modal, so it could be opened from multiple entry points across the platform
  • Planned an AI-assisted flow for flagging and reporting inappropriate reviews

Impact

The project was not shipped, but it set the direction for how cross-app review management should work at scale.

Screens

Dashboard & navigation

Review management modal

AI-assisted reporting

Bottom line

The reply UI wasn't the hard part. A developer with many apps needs to see reviews aggregated in a way that doesn't require switching between ten different contexts. Getting that architecture right was the actual design problem. The AI reporting flow raised a question I didn't have a clean answer to: how much do you trust a model's judgment on something that has real consequences for another person?
